121	 PROPOSED COMPLIANCE ORDER
   122	Pursuant to 49 United States Code § 60118, the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety
   123	Administration (PHMSA) proposes to issue to BP a Compliance Order incorporating the
   124	following remedial requirements to ensure the compliance of BP with the pipeline safety
   125	regulations:
   126	A.
   127	
   128	In regard to Item 1 of the Notice, pertaining to BP’s failure to properly inspect its
   129	right-of-way (ROW), BP must:
   130	1. Develop a plan to clear the ROW for the patrol area known as Pipeline
   131	Segment Brom TN Ave BOCI 6 located within the City of Cincinnati, Ohio
   132	and submit this to Gregory A. Ochs, Director of Central Region for review
   133	and approval within 30 days of receipt of the Final Order. Within 120 days of
   134	approval of the plan, BP must submit evidence of proper clearing of the
   135	referenced section along with the most recent Ground Patrol Report Form #F195.412(a) GP for this section demonstrating that a successful patrol was
   136	performed.
   137	2. Review the effectiveness of its procedures and personnel performing the
   138	procedures regarding the patrol of its ROW. This review shall examine the
   139	communication between personnel responsible for the scheduling of clearing
   140	and those that are performing patrols, as well as local technicians that
   141	frequently travel the right of way to ensure that all parties are aware of signs
   142	of deficient conditions. Documentation of this review and any revised
   143	procedures shall be submitted to Gregory A. Ochs, Director of Central Region
   144	for review and approval within 60 days of receipt of the Final Order.
   145	
   146	B.
   147	
   148	It is requested that BP maintain documentation of the safety improvement costs
   149	associated with fulfilling this Compliance Order and submit the total to Gregory A.
   150	Ochs, Director of Central Region, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety
   151	Administration. It is requested that these costs be reported in two categories: (1)
   152	total cost associated with preparation/revision of plans, procedures, studies and
   153	analyses, and (2) total cost associated with replacements, additions and other
   154	changes to pipeline infrastructure.
